rationale: In Old English legal texts, CEORL (a freeman of the lowest rank) is frequently contrasted with nobles or clergy, and the gloss "simple" here refers to a person of humble or low status/wit — i.e., a common, simple person lacking sophistication — which aligns best with simpleton.n.01 (a person lacking intelligence or common sense) rather than the botanical sense of simple.n.01. The legal attestations (L. Eth., L. R.) confirm a social/personal characterization of an ordinary, undistinguished man.
